<h4 id="istioctl-kube-inject Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Update resources on the fly before applying.
  kubectl apply -f &lt;(istioctl kube-inject -f &lt;resource.yaml&gt;)

  # Create a persistent version of the deployment with Istio sidecar injected.
  istioctl kube-inject -f deployment.yaml -o deployment-injected.yaml

  # Update an existing deployment.
  kubectl get deployment -o yaml | istioctl kube-inject -f - | kubectl apply -f -

  # Capture cluster configuration for later use with kube-inject
  kubectl -n istio-system get cm istio-sidecar-injector  -o jsonpath=&#34;{.data.config}&#34; &gt; /tmp/inj-template.tmpl
  kubectl -n istio-system get cm istio -o jsonpath=&#34;{.data.mesh}&#34; &gt; /tmp/mesh.yaml
  kubectl -n istio-system get cm istio-sidecar-injector -o jsonpath=&#34;{.data.values}&#34; &gt; /tmp/values.json

  # Use kube-inject based on captured configuration
  istioctl kube-inject -f samples/bookinfo/platform/kube/bookinfo.yaml \
    --injectConfigFile /tmp/inj-template.tmpl \
    --meshConfigFile /tmp/mesh.yaml \
    --valuesFile /tmp/values.json

</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-manifest-generate Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Generate a default Istio installation
  istioctl manifest generate

  # Enable Tracing
  istioctl manifest generate --set meshConfig.enableTracing=true

  # Generate the demo profile
  istioctl manifest generate --set profile=demo

  # Write the manifest to a file instead of stdout (avoids shell redirection; works where no shell is available)
  istioctl manifest generate -o /shared/istio.yaml

  # To override a setting that includes dots, escape them with a backslash (\).  Your shell may require enclosing quotes.
  istioctl manifest generate --set &#34;values.sidecarInjectorWebhook.injectedAnnotations.container\.apparmor\.security\.beta\.kubernetes\.io/istio-proxy=runtime/default&#34;

</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-proxy-config-all Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve summary about all configuration for a given pod from Envoy.
  istioctl proxy-config all &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt;

  # Retrieve summary about all configuration for a pod under a deployment from Envoy.
  istioctl proxy-config all deployment/&lt;deployment-name[.namespace]&gt;

  # Retrieve full cluster dump as JSON
  istioctl proxy-config all &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; -o json

  # Retrieve full cluster dump with short syntax
  istioctl pc a &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt;

  # Retrieve cluster summary without using Kubernetes API
  ssh &lt;user@hostname&gt; &#39;curl localhost:15000/config_dump&#39; &gt; envoy-config.json
  istioctl proxy-config all --file envoy-config.json

</code></pre>

  # Retrieve full endpoint with a address (172.17.0.2).

  # Retrieve full endpoint with a cluster name (outbound|9411||zipkin.istio-system.svc.cluster.local).
  istioctl proxy-config endpoint &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; --cluster &#34;outbound|9411||zipkin.istio-system.svc.cluster.local&#34; -o json
  # Retrieve full endpoint with the status (healthy).
  istioctl proxy-config endpoint &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; --status healthy -ojson

  # Retrieve endpoint summary without using Kubernetes API
  ssh &lt;user@hostname&gt; &#39;curl localhost:15000/clusters?format=json&#39; &gt; envoy-clusters.json
  istioctl proxy-config endpoints --file envoy-clusters.json

</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-proxy-config-log Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve information about logging levels for a given pod from Envoy.
  istioctl proxy-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt;

  # Update levels of the all loggers
  istioctl proxy-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; --level none

  # Update levels of the specified loggers.
  istioctl proxy-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; --level http:debug,redis:debug

  # Reset levels of all the loggers to default value (warning).
  istioctl proxy-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; -r

</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-proxy-status Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve sync status for all Envoys in a mesh
  istioctl proxy-status

  # Retrieve sync status for Envoys in a specific namespace
  istioctl proxy-status --namespace foo

  # Retrieve sync diff for a single Envoy and Istiod
  istioctl proxy-status istio-egressgateway-59585c5b9c-ndc59.istio-system

  # SECURITY OPTIONS

  # Retrieve proxy status information directly from the control plane, using token security
  # (This is the usual way to get the proxy-status with an out-of-cluster control plane.)
  istioctl ps --xds-address istio.cloudprovider.example.com:15012

  # Retrieve proxy status information via Kubernetes config, using token security
  # (This is the usual way to get the proxy-status with an in-cluster control plane.)
  istioctl proxy-status

  # Retrieve proxy status information directly from the control plane, using RSA certificate security
  # (Certificates must be obtained before this step.  The --cert-dir flag lets istioctl bypass the Kubernetes API server.)
  istioctl ps --xds-address istio.example.com:15012 --cert-dir ~/.istio-certs

  # Retrieve proxy status information via XDS from specific control plane in multi-control plane in-cluster configuration
  # (Select a specific control plane in an in-cluster canary Istio configuration.)
  istioctl ps --xds-label istio.io/rev=default

  # Show the status of a specific proxy in JSON format
  istioctl proxy-status --output json
</code></pre>

<h3 id="istioctl-tag">istioctl tag</h3>
<p>Command group used to interact with revision tags. Revision tags allow for the creation of mutable aliases
referring to control plane revisions for sidecar injection.</p>
<p>With revision tags, rather than relabeling a namespace from &#34;istio.io/rev=revision-a&#34; to &#34;istio.io/rev=revision-b&#34; to
change which control plane revision handles injection, it&#39;s possible to create a revision tag &#34;prod&#34; and label our
namespace &#34;istio.io/rev=prod&#34;. The &#34;prod&#34; revision tag could point to &#34;1-7-6&#34; initially and then be changed to point to &#34;1-8-1&#34;
at some later point.</p>
<p>This allows operators to change which Istio control plane revision should handle injection for a namespace or set of namespaces
without manual relabeling of the &#34;istio.io/rev&#34; tag.
</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>istioctl tag [flags]
</code></pre>
<table class="command-flags">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Flags</th>
<th>Shorthand</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>--as &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Username to impersonate for the operation. User could be a regular user or a service account in a namespace  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-group &lt;stringArray&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Group to impersonate for the operation, this flag can be repeated to specify multiple groups.  (default `[]`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-uid &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>UID to impersonate for the operation.  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--context &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes configuration context  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--istioNamespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-i</code></td>
<td>Istio system namespace  (default `istio-system`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeclient-timeout &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes client timeout as a time.Duration string, defaults to 15 seconds.  (default `15s`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeconfig &lt;string&gt;</code></td>

<td>Kubernetes configuration file  (default ``)</td>

<h3 id="istioctl-tag-generate">istioctl tag generate</h3>
<p>Create a revision tag and output to the command&#39;s stdout. Tag an Istio control plane revision for use with namespace istio.io/rev
injection labels.</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>istioctl tag generate &lt;revision-tag&gt; [flags]
</code></pre>
<table class="command-flags">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Flags</th>
<th>Shorthand</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>--as &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Username to impersonate for the operation. User could be a regular user or a service account in a namespace  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-group &lt;stringArray&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Group to impersonate for the operation, this flag can be repeated to specify multiple groups.  (default `[]`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-uid &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>UID to impersonate for the operation.  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--auto-inject-namespaces</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>If set to true, the sidecars should be automatically injected into all namespaces by default </td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--context &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes configuration context  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--istioNamespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-i</code></td>
<td>Istio system namespace  (default `istio-system`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeclient-timeout &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes client timeout as a time.Duration string, defaults to 15 seconds.  (default `15s`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeconfig &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-c</code></td>
<td>Kubernetes configuration file  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--manifests &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-d</code></td>
<td>Specify a path to a directory of charts and profiles
(e.g. ~/Downloads/istio-1.30.0/manifests).  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--namespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-n</code></td>
<td>Kubernetes namespace  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--overwrite</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>If true, allow revision tags to be overwritten, otherwise reject revision tag updates that
overwrite existing revision tags. </td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--revision &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-r</code></td>
<td>Control plane revision to reference from a given revision tag  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--skip-confirmation</code></td>
<td><code>-y</code></td>
<td>The skipConfirmation determines whether the user is prompted for confirmation.
If set to true, the user is not prompted and a Yes response is assumed in all cases. </td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--vklog &lt;Level&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>number for the log level verbosity. Like -v flag. ex: --vklog=9  (default `0`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--webhook-name &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Name to use for a revision tag&#39;s mutating webhook configuration.  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h4 id="istioctl-tag-generate Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Create a revision tag from the &#34;1-8-0&#34; revision
  istioctl tag generate prod --revision 1-8-0 &gt; tag.yaml

  # Apply the tag to cluster
  kubectl apply -f tag.yaml

  # Point namespace &#34;test-ns&#34; at the revision pointed to by the &#34;prod&#34; revision tag
  kubectl label ns test-ns istio.io/rev=prod

  # Rollout namespace &#34;test-ns&#34; to update workloads to the &#34;1-8-0&#34; revision
  kubectl rollout restart deployments -n test-ns

</code></pre>

<h3 id="istioctl-tag-remove">istioctl tag remove</h3>
<p>Remove Istio control plane revision tag.</p>
<p>Removing a revision tag should be done with care. Removing a revision tag will disrupt sidecar injection in namespaces
that reference the tag in an &#34;istio.io/rev&#34; label. Verify that there are no remaining namespaces referencing a
revision tag before removing using the &#34;istioctl tag list&#34; command.
</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>istioctl tag remove &lt;revision-tag&gt; [flags]
</code></pre>
<div class="aliases">

<h4 id="istioctl-tag-set Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Create a revision tag from the &#34;1-8-0&#34; revision
  istioctl tag set prod --revision 1-8-0

  # Point namespace &#34;test-ns&#34; at the revision pointed to by the &#34;prod&#34; revision tag
  kubectl label ns test-ns istio.io/rev=prod

  # Change the revision tag to reference the &#34;1-8-1&#34; revision
  istioctl tag set prod --revision 1-8-1 --overwrite

  # Make revision &#34;1-8-1&#34; the default revision, both resulting in that revision handling injection for &#34;istio-injection=enabled&#34;
  # and validating resources cluster-wide
  istioctl tag set default --revision 1-8-1

  # Rollout namespace &#34;test-ns&#34; to update workloads to the &#34;1-8-1&#34; revision
  kubectl rollout restart deployments -n test-ns

</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-uninstall Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Uninstall a single control plane by revision
  istioctl uninstall --revision foo

  # Uninstall a single control plane by iop file
  istioctl uninstall -f iop.yaml
  
  # Uninstall all control planes and shared resources
  istioctl uninstall --purge
</code></pre>

<h4 id="istioctl-validate Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Validate bookinfo-gateway.yaml
  istioctl validate -f samples/bookinfo/networking/bookinfo-gateway.yaml

  # Validate bookinfo-gateway.yaml with shorthand syntax
  istioctl v -f samples/bookinfo/networking/bookinfo-gateway.yaml

  # Validate all yaml files under samples/bookinfo/networking directory
  istioctl validate -f samples/bookinfo/networking

  # Validate current deployments under &#39;default&#39; namespace within the cluster
  kubectl get deployments -o yaml | istioctl validate -f -

  # Validate current services under &#39;default&#39; namespace within the cluster
  kubectl get services -o yaml | istioctl validate -f -

  # Also see the related command &#39;istioctl analyze&#39;
  istioctl analyze samples/bookinfo/networking/bookinfo-gateway.yaml

</code></pre>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h4 id="istioctl-ztunnel-config-log Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve information about logging levels from all Ztunnel pods
 istioctl ztunnel-config log

 # Update levels of the all loggers for a specific Ztunnel pod
 istioctl ztunnel-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; --level off

 # Update levels of the specified loggers for all Ztunnl pods
 istioctl ztunnel-config log --level access:debug,info

 # Reset levels of all the loggers to default value (warning)  for a specific Ztunnel pod.
 istioctl ztunnel-config log &lt;pod-name[.namespace]&gt; -r

</code></pre>

<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve summary about services configuration for a randomly chosen ztunnel.
  istioctl ztunnel-config services

  # Retrieve full services dump of workloads for a given Ztunnel instance.
  istioctl ztunnel-config services &lt;ztunnel-name[.namespace]&gt; -o json

</code></pre>
<h3 id="istioctl-ztunnel-config-workload">istioctl ztunnel-config workload</h3>
<p>Retrieve information about workload configuration for the Ztunnel instance.</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>istioctl ztunnel-config workload [&lt;type&gt;/]&lt;name&gt;[.&lt;namespace&gt;] [flags]
</code></pre>
<div class="aliases">
<pre class="language-bash"><code>istioctl ztunnel-config w [&lt;type&gt;/]&lt;name&gt;[.&lt;namespace&gt;] [flags]
istioctl ztunnel-config workloads [&lt;type&gt;/]&lt;name&gt;[.&lt;namespace&gt;] [flags]
</code></pre></div>
<table class="command-flags">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Flags</th>
<th>Shorthand</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>--address &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Filter workloads by address field  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Username to impersonate for the operation. User could be a regular user or a service account in a namespace  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-group &lt;stringArray&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Group to impersonate for the operation, this flag can be repeated to specify multiple groups.  (default `[]`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--as-uid &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>UID to impersonate for the operation.  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--context &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes configuration context  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--file &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-f</code></td>
<td>Ztunnel config dump JSON file  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--istioNamespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-i</code></td>
<td>Istio system namespace  (default `istio-system`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeclient-timeout &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Kubernetes client timeout as a time.Duration string, defaults to 15 seconds.  (default `15s`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--kubeconfig &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-c</code></td>
<td>Kubernetes configuration file  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--namespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-n</code></td>
<td>Kubernetes namespace  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--node &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Filter workloads by node field  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--output &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td><code>-o</code></td>
<td>Output format: one of json|yaml|short  (default `short`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--proxy-admin-port &lt;int&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Ztunnel proxy admin port  (default `15000`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--vklog &lt;Level&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>number for the log level verbosity. Like -v flag. ex: --vklog=9  (default `0`)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--workload-namespace &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Filter workloads by namespace field  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>--workload-node &lt;string&gt;</code></td>
<td></td>
<td>Filter workloads by node  (default ``)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h4 id="istioctl-ztunnel-config-workload Examples">Examples</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>  # Retrieve summary about workload configuration for a randomly chosen ztunnel.
  istioctl ztunnel-config workload

  # Retrieve summary of workloads on node XXXX for a given Ztunnel instance.
  istioctl ztunnel-config workload &lt;ztunnel-name[.namespace]&gt; --node ambient-worker

  # Retrieve full workload dump of workloads with address XXXX for a given Ztunnel instance.
  istioctl ztunnel-config workload &lt;ztunnel-name[.namespace]&gt; --address 0.0.0.0 -o json

  # Retrieve Ztunnel config dump separately and inspect from file.
  kubectl exec -it $ZTUNNEL -n istio-system -- curl localhost:15000/config_dump &gt; ztunnel-config.json
  istioctl ztunnel-config workloads --file ztunnel-config.json

  # Retrieve workload summary for a specific namespace
  istioctl ztunnel-config workloads &lt;ztunnel-name[.namespace]&gt; --workload-namespace foo

  # Retrieve workload info for a specific workload pod (auto-resolves to its ztunnel).
  istioctl ztunnel-config workload &lt;workload-pod-name[.namespace]&gt;

</code></pre>
<h2 id="envvars">Environment variables</h2>
These environment variables affect the behavior of the <code>istioctl</code> command. 
<table class="envvars">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Variable Name</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Default Value</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr id='ambient-enable-baggage'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-baggage'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_BAGGAGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, enables waypoints to use baggage header to discover and propagate peer metadata for metrics.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-dry-run-authorization-policy'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-dry-run-authorization-policy'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, ztunnel will be configured with dry-run authorizationPolicies. Ensure ztunnel is 1.29 or above before enabling this feature. Older ztunnel will accept dry-run policies, but enforce them instead of only logging.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-multi-network'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-multi-network'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, the multi-network functionality will be enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-multi-network-ingress'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-multi-network-ingress'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK_INGRESS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true and AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK is also true, it will enable ingress gateways to route requests to clusters on remote networks while by default ingress gateways will keep traffic local.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-multi-network-waypoint'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-multi-network-waypoint'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK_WAYPOINT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true and AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK is also true, it will enable waypoints to route requests to clusters on remote networks, while by default waypoints will keep traffic local.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-status'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-status'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_STATUS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, status messages for ambient mode will be written to resources. Currently, this does not do leader election, so may be unsafe to enable with multiple replicas.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-enable-tls-proxy-http-metrics'>
<td><a href='#ambient-enable-tls-proxy-http-metrics'><code>AMBIENT_ENABLE_TLS_PROXY_HTTP_METRICS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, enables waypoints to register HTTP metrics for cross-cluster requests when using protocols like TLS or PROXY.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ambient-scoped-address-pushes'>
<td><a href='#ambient-scoped-address-pushes'><code>AMBIENT_SCOPED_ADDRESS_PUSHES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, ambient Address updates only trigger pushes for waypoints whose attached services or workloads changed, and are skipped entirely for sidecar and gateway proxies. If disabled, every Address update triggers a full LDS/CDS/EDS push to all waypoints and an RDS push to all proxies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='auto-gke-detection'>
<td><a href='#auto-gke-detection'><code>AUTO_GKE_DETECTION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, GKE will be detected automatically.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='blocked-cidrs-in-jwks-uris'>
<td><a href='#blocked-cidrs-in-jwks-uris'><code>BLOCKED_CIDRS_IN_JWKS_URIS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of CIDR ranges that are blocked in JWKS URIs (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.1.0/24).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='blocked-cidrs-in-wasm-fetch'>
<td><a href='#blocked-cidrs-in-wasm-fetch'><code>BLOCKED_CIDRS_IN_WASM_FETCH</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of CIDR ranges that are blocked when fetching Wasm modules (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.1.0/24).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='ca-trusted-node-accounts'>
<td><a href='#ca-trusted-node-accounts'><code>CA_TRUSTED_NODE_ACCOUNTS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, the list of service accounts that are allowed to use node authentication for CSRs. Node authentication allows an identity to create CSRs on behalf of other identities, but only if there is a pod running on the same node with that identity. This is intended for use with node proxies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='cert-signer-domain'>
<td><a href='#cert-signer-domain'><code>CERT_SIGNER_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>The cert signer domain info</td>
</tr>
<tr id='cluster-id'>
<td><a href='#cluster-id'><code>CLUSTER_ID</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>Kubernetes</code></td>
<td>Defines the cluster and service registry that this Istiod instance belongs to</td>
</tr>
<tr id='compliance-policy'>
<td><a href='#compliance-policy'><code>COMPLIANCE_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, applies policy-specific restrictions over all existing TLS
settings, including in-mesh mTLS and external TLS. Valid values are:

* &#39;&#39; or unset places no additional restrictions.
* &#39;fips-140-2&#39; which enforces TLS v1.2 and a subset of cipher suites
overriding any user preferences or defaults for all runtime components,
including Envoy, gRPC Go SDK, and gRPC C++ SDK.
* &#39;fips-140-3&#39; which enforces TLS v1.2 or v1.3, FIPS-compliant cipher
suites (ECDHE_[RSA|ECDSA]_WITH_AES_*_GCM_SHA* for TLS 1.2, AES-GCM for
TLS 1.3), and P-256 or P-384 curves. On the Envoy proxy side, this uses
the native FIPS_202205 compliance policy. Overrides any user preferences
or defaults for all runtime components, including Envoy, gRPC Go SDK,
and gRPC C++ SDK.
* &#39;pqc&#39; which enforces post-quantum-safe key exchange X25519MLKEM768, TLS v1.3
and cipher suites TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 overriding
any user preferences or defaults for all runtime components, including Envoy,
gRPC Go SDK, and gRPC C++ SDK. This policy is experimental.

WARNING: Setting compliance policy in the control plane is a necessary but
not a sufficient requirement to achieve compliance. There are additional
steps necessary to claim compliance, including using the validated
cryptographic modules (please consult
https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/intro/arch_overview/security/ssl#fips-140-2).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='debug-endpoint-auth-allowed-namespaces'>
<td><a href='#debug-endpoint-auth-allowed-namespaces'><code>DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of namespaces to allow access to debug endpoints. Only used if ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH is enabled. The system namespaceis always authorized.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='disable-shadow-host-suffix'>
<td><a href='#disable-shadow-host-suffix'><code>DISABLE_SHADOW_HOST_SUFFIX</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If disabled, the shadow host suffix will be added to the hostnames of the mirrored requests.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='disable-track-remaining-cb-metrics'>
<td><a href='#disable-track-remaining-cb-metrics'><code>DISABLE_TRACK_REMAINING_CB_METRICS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If disabled, the remaining metrics for circuit breakers will not be tracked.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-100-continue-headers'>
<td><a href='#enable-100-continue-headers'><code>ENABLE_100_CONTINUE_HEADERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will proxy 100-continue headers as is</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-ca-server'>
<td><a href='#enable-ca-server'><code>ENABLE_CA_SERVER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to false, will not create CA server in istiod.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-cluster-trust-bundle-api'>
<td><a href='#enable-cluster-trust-bundle-api'><code>ENABLE_CLUSTER_TRUST_BUNDLE_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, uses the ClusterTrustBundle API instead of ConfigMaps to store the root certificate in the cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-debug-endpoint-auth'>
<td><a href='#enable-debug-endpoint-auth'><code>ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Enforce namespace-based authorization on debug endpoints. Non-system namespaces restricted to config_dump/ndsz/edsz for same-namespace proxies only.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-debug-on-http'>
<td><a href='#enable-debug-on-http'><code>ENABLE_DEBUG_ON_HTTP</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to false, the debug interface will not be enabled, recommended for production</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-enhanced-destinationrule-merge'>
<td><a href='#enable-enhanced-destinationrule-merge'><code>ENABLE_ENHANCED_DESTINATIONRULE_MERGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Istio merge destinationrules considering their exportTo fields, they will be kept as independent rules if the exportTos are not equal.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-gateway-api-httproute-auth'>
<td><a href='#enable-gateway-api-httproute-auth'><code>ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_HTTPROUTE_AUTH</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, support targeting Gateway API HTTPRoute resources with AuthorizationPolicy</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-gateway-api-inference-extension'>
<td><a href='#enable-gateway-api-inference-extension'><code>ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_INFERENCE_EXTENSION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, support gateway inference extension routing apis</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-gateway-api-manual-deployment'>
<td><a href='#enable-gateway-api-manual-deployment'><code>ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_MANUAL_DEPLOYMENT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, allows users to bind Gateway API resources to existing gateway deployments.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-hcm-internal-networks'>
<td><a href='#enable-hcm-internal-networks'><code>ENABLE_HCM_INTERNAL_NETWORKS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enable, endpoints defined in mesh networks will be configured as internal addresses in Http Connection Manager</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-ingress-waypoint-routing'>
<td><a href='#enable-ingress-waypoint-routing'><code>ENABLE_INGRESS_WAYPOINT_ROUTING</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Gateways will call service waypoints if the &#39;istio.io/ingress-use-waypoint&#39; label set on the Service.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-layered-waypoint-authorization-policies'>
<td><a href='#enable-layered-waypoint-authorization-policies'><code>ENABLE_LAYERED_WAYPOINT_AUTHORIZATION_POLICIES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, selector based authorization policies will be enforced as L4 policies in front of the waypoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-lazy-sidecar-evaluation'>
<td><a href='#enable-lazy-sidecar-evaluation'><code>ENABLE_LAZY_SIDECAR_EVALUATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will only compute sidecar resources when actually used</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-leader-election'>
<td><a href='#enable-leader-election'><code>ENABLE_LEADER_ELECTION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled (default), starts a leader election client and gains leadership before executing controllers. If false, it assumes that only one instance of istiod is running and skips leader election.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-locality-weighted-lb-config'>
<td><a href='#enable-locality-weighted-lb-config'><code>ENABLE_LOCALITY_WEIGHTED_LB_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, always set LocalityWeightedLbConfig for a cluster,  otherwise only apply it when locality lb is specified by DestinationRule for a service</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-mcs-auto-export'>
<td><a href='#enable-mcs-auto-export'><code>ENABLE_MCS_AUTO_EXPORT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will automatically generate Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) ServiceExport resources for every service in the mesh. Services defined to be cluster-local in MeshConfig are excluded.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-mcs-cluster-local'>
<td><a href='#enable-mcs-cluster-local'><code>ENABLE_MCS_CLUSTER_LOCAL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will treat the host `&lt;svc&gt;.&lt;namespace&gt;.svc.cluster.local` as defined by the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) spec. In this mode, requests to `cluster.local` will be routed to only those endpoints residing within the same cluster as the client. Requires that both ENABLE_MCS_SERVICE_DISCOVERY and ENABLE_MCS_HOST also be enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-mcs-host'>
<td><a href='#enable-mcs-host'><code>ENABLE_MCS_HOST</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will configure a Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) host (&lt;svc&gt;.&lt;namespace&gt;.svc.clusterset.local) for each service exported (via ServiceExport) in at least one cluster. Clients must, however, be able to successfully lookup these DNS hosts. That means that either Istio DNS interception must be enabled or an MCS controller must be used. Requires that ENABLE_MCS_SERVICE_DISCOVERY also be enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-mcs-service-discovery'>
<td><a href='#enable-mcs-service-discovery'><code>ENABLE_MCS_SERVICE_DISCOVERY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will enable Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) service discovery mode. In this mode, service endpoints in a cluster will only be discoverable within the same cluster unless explicitly exported via ServiceExport.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-multicluster-headless'>
<td><a href='#enable-multicluster-headless'><code>ENABLE_MULTICLUSTER_HEADLESS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, the DNS name table for a headless service will resolve to same-network endpoints in any cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-native-sidecars'>
<td><a href='#enable-native-sidecars'><code>ENABLE_NATIVE_SIDECARS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>auto</code></td>
<td>If set to true, use Kubernetes native sidecar container support. Requires SidecarContainer feature flag. Set to true to unconditionally enable, false to unconditionally disable. Set to auto to automatically enable for supported scenarios</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-probe-keepalive-connections'>
<td><a href='#enable-probe-keepalive-connections'><code>ENABLE_PROBE_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, readiness probes will keep the connection from pilot-agent to the application alive. This mirrors older Istio versions&#39; behaviors, but not kubelet&#39;s.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-proxy-find-pod-by-ip'>
<td><a href='#enable-proxy-find-pod-by-ip'><code>ENABLE_PROXY_FIND_POD_BY_IP</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the pod controller will allow finding pods matching proxies by IP if it fails to find them by name.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-selector-based-k8s-gateway-policy'>
<td><a href='#enable-selector-based-k8s-gateway-policy'><code>ENABLE_SELECTOR_BASED_K8S_GATEWAY_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If disabled, Gateway API gateways will ignore workloadSelector policies, onlyapplying policies that select the gateway with a targetRef.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-tls-on-sidecar-ingress'>
<td><a href='#enable-tls-on-sidecar-ingress'><code>ENABLE_TLS_ON_SIDECAR_INGRESS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the TLS configuration on Sidecar.ingress will take effect</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-vtprotobuf'>
<td><a href='#enable-vtprotobuf'><code>ENABLE_VTPROTOBUF</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, will use optimized vtprotobuf based marshaling. Requires a build with -tags=vtprotobuf.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-wildcard-host-service-entries-for-tls'>
<td><a href='#enable-wildcard-host-service-entries-for-tls'><code>ENABLE_WILDCARD_HOST_SERVICE_ENTRIES_FOR_TLS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, ServiceEntries with wildcard hosts and dynamic dns resolution will be allowed for TLS traffic. This is a security risk, susceptible to SNI spoofing, and should be used with caution. Only consider using this feature if the client is trusted and you understand the risks.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='enable-xds-api-generator-auth'>
<td><a href='#enable-xds-api-generator-auth'><code>ENABLE_XDS_API_GENERATOR_AUTH</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the XDS &#39;api&#39; generator (MCP-over-xDS config serving) is restricted to callers with a verified control-plane (root namespace) identity. Prevents an unauthenticated client on the plaintext xDS port, or a workload in an unrelated namespace on the mTLS port, from reading cluster-wide Istio config.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='envoy-status-port-enable-proxy-protocol'>
<td><a href='#envoy-status-port-enable-proxy-protocol'><code>ENVOY_STATUS_PORT_ENABLE_PROXY_PROTOCOL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Envoy will support requests with proxy protocol on its status port</td>
</tr>
<tr id='external-istiod'>

<tr id='istioctl-xds-port'>

<tr id='istio-agent-enable-wasm-remote-load-conversion'>

<tr id='istio-delta-xds'>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-dual-stack'>
<td><a href='#istio-dual-stack'><code>ISTIO_DUAL_STACK</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Istio will enable the Dual Stack feature.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-enable-controller-queue-metrics'>
<td><a href='#istio-enable-controller-queue-metrics'><code>ISTIO_ENABLE_CONTROLLER_QUEUE_METRICS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-enable-http2-probing'>

<td>Boolean</td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-enable-ipv4-outbound-listener-for-ipv6-clusters'>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-gprc-maxrecvmsgsize'>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-gprc-maxstreams'>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-kube-client-content-type'>

<tr id='istio-kube-header-timeout'>

<td><code>1m30s</code></td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-kube-request-timeout'>
<td><a href='#istio-kube-request-timeout'><code>ISTIO_KUBE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>15m0s</code></td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-multiroot-mesh'>

<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-ipv4-loopback-cidr'>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-owner-groups'>
<td><a href='#istio-outbound-owner-groups'><code>ISTIO_OUTBOUND_OWNER_GROUPS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>

A group can be specified either by name or by a numeric GID.
The wildcard character &#34;*&#34; can be used to configure redirection of traffic from all groups.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-owner-groups-exclude'>

<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of groups whose outgoing traffic is to be excluded from redirection to Envoy.
A group can be specified either by name or by a numeric GID.
Only applies when traffic from all groups (i.e. &#34;*&#34;) is being redirected to Envoy.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-prometheus-annotations'>
<td><a href='#istio-prometheus-annotations'><code>ISTIO_PROMETHEUS_ANNOTATIONS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-wasm-max-binary-size-bytes'>
<td><a href='#istio-wasm-max-binary-size-bytes'><code>ISTIO_WASM_MAX_BINARY_SIZE_BYTES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>

</tr>
<tr id='istio-watch-namespace'>
<td><a href='#istio-watch-namespace'><code>ISTIO_WATCH_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>

</tr>
<tr id='jwks-resolver-insecure-skip-verify'>
<td><a href='#jwks-resolver-insecure-skip-verify'><code>JWKS_RESOLVER_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY</code></a></td>

</tr>
<tr id='label-canonical-services-for-mesh-external-service-entries'>
<td><a href='#label-canonical-services-for-mesh-external-service-entries'><code>LABEL_CANONICAL_SERVICES_FOR_MESH_EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ENTRIES</code></a></td>

</tr>
<tr id='local-cluster-secret-watcher'>

<td>Boolean</td>

</tr>

<td>String</td>
<td><code>v1alpha1</code></td>
<td>The version to be used for the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) API.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='metrics-localhost-access-only'>
<td><a href='#metrics-localhost-access-only'><code>METRICS_LOCALHOST_ACCESS_ONLY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>This will disable metrics endpoint from outside of the pod, allowing only localhost access.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='mutex-profile-fraction'>
<td><a href='#mutex-profile-fraction'><code>MUTEX_PROFILE_FRACTION</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1000</code></td>
<td>If set to a non-zero value, enables mutex profiling a rate of 1/MUTEX_PROFILE_FRACTION events. For example, &#39;1000&#39; will record 0.1% of events. Set to 0 to disable entirely.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-agent-merge-envoy-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-agent-merge-envoy-stats'><code>PILOT_AGENT_MERGE_ENVOY_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If false, pilot agent will not merge Envoy stats in the agent stats endpoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-allow-any-dynamic-dns-max-hosts'>
<td><a href='#pilot-allow-any-dynamic-dns-max-hosts'><code>PILOT_ALLOW_ANY_DYNAMIC_DNS_MAX_HOSTS</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1024</code></td>
<td>Maximum number of hosts kept in the dynamic forward proxy DNS cache for ALLOW_ANY_DYNAMIC_DNS outbound traffic mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-allow-sidecar-service-inbound-listener-merge'>
<td><a href='#pilot-allow-sidecar-service-inbound-listener-merge'><code>PILOT_ALLOW_SIDECAR_SERVICE_INBOUND_LISTENER_MERGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If set, it allows creating inbound listeners for service ports and sidecar ingress listeners </td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-analysis-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-analysis-interval'><code>PILOT_ANALYSIS_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>If analysis is enabled, pilot will run istio analyzers using this value as interval in seconds Istio Resources</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-auto-allow-waypoint-policy'>
<td><a href='#pilot-auto-allow-waypoint-policy'><code>PILOT_AUTO_ALLOW_WAYPOINT_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, zTunnel will receive synthetic authorization policies for each workload ALLOW the Waypoint&#39;s identity. Unless other ALLOW policies are created, this effectively denies traffic that doesn&#39;t go through the waypoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-auto-send-unhealthy-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-auto-send-unhealthy-endpoints'><code>PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include unhealthy endpoints in EDS pushes by default. Unhealthy endpoints are excluded only when OutlierDetection is configured with minHealthPercent &gt; 0, to prevent Envoy from routing traffic to non-ready endpoints when the panic threshold is triggered.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ca-cert-configmap'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ca-cert-configmap'><code>PILOT_CA_CERT_CONFIGMAP</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca-root-cert</code></td>
<td>The name of the ConfigMap that stores the Root CA Certificate that is used by istiod</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-cert-provider'>
<td><a href='#pilot-cert-provider'><code>PILOT_CERT_PROVIDER</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istiod</code></td>
<td>The provider of Pilot DNS certificate. K8S RA will be used for k8s.io/NAME. &#39;istiod&#39; value will sign using Istio build in CA. Other values will not not generate TLS certs, but still  distribute ./etc/certs/root-cert.pem. Only used if custom certificates are not mounted.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-convert-sidecar-scope-concurrency'>
<td><a href='#pilot-convert-sidecar-scope-concurrency'><code>PILOT_CONVERT_SIDECAR_SCOPE_CONCURRENCY</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td>Deprecated, superseded by ENABLE_LAZY_SIDECAR_EVALUATION. Used to adjust the concurrency of SidecarScope conversions. When istiod is deployed on a multi-core CPU server, increasing this value will help to use the CPU to accelerate configuration push, but it also means that istiod will consume more CPU resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-crl-configmap'>
<td><a href='#pilot-crl-configmap'><code>PILOT_CRL_CONFIGMAP</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca-crl</code></td>
<td>The name of the ConfigMap that stores the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) for a plugged-in CA</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-debounce-after'>
<td><a href='#pilot-debounce-after'><code>PILOT_DEBOUNCE_AFTER</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>100ms</code></td>
<td>The delay added to config/registry events for debouncing. This will delay the push by at least this interval. If no change is detected within this period, the push will happen,  otherwise we&#39;ll keep delaying until things settle, up to a max of PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-debounce-max'>
<td><a href='#pilot-debounce-max'><code>PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>The maximum amount of time to wait for events while debouncing. If events keep showing up with no breaks for this time, we&#39;ll trigger a push.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-disable-mx-alpn'>
<td><a href='#pilot-disable-mx-alpn'><code>PILOT_DISABLE_MX_ALPN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will not put istio-peer-exchange ALPN into TLS handshake configuration.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-dns-cares-udp-max-queries'>
<td><a href='#pilot-dns-cares-udp-max-queries'><code>PILOT_DNS_CARES_UDP_MAX_QUERIES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>100</code></td>
<td>Sets the `udp_max_queries` option in Envoy for the Cares DNS resolver. Defaults to 0, an unlimited number of queries. See `extensions.network.dns_resolver.cares.v3.CaresDnsResolverConfig` in https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/extensions/network/dns_resolver/cares/v3/cares_dns_resolver.proto and `ARES_OPT_UDP_MAX_QUERIES` in https://c-ares.org/docs/ares_init.html</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-dns-jitter-duration'>
<td><a href='#pilot-dns-jitter-duration'><code>PILOT_DNS_JITTER_DURATION</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>100ms</code></td>
<td>Jitter added to periodic DNS resolution</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-draining-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-draining-label'><code>PILOT_DRAINING_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/draining</code></td>
<td>If not empty, endpoints with the label value present will be sent with status DRAINING.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-absolute-fqdn-vhost-domain'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-absolute-fqdn-vhost-domain'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ABSOLUTE_FQDN_VHOST_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If set to false, Istio will not add the absolute FQDN variant (e.g., my-service.my-ns.svc.cluster.local.) to the domains list for VirtualHost entries.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-agentgateway'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-agentgateway'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the istio-agentgateway GatewayClass will be enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-alpha-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-alpha-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, support for alpha APIs in the Kubernetes gateway-api (github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api) will  be enabled. In addition to this being enabled, the gateway-api CRDs need to be installed.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-alpn-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-alpn-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ALPN_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add Istio ALPN filters, required for proper protocol sniffing.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ambient'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ambient'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AMBIENT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, ambient mode can be used. Individual flags configure fine grained enablement; this must be enabled for any ambient functionality.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ambient-waypoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ambient-waypoints'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AMBIENT_WAYPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, controllers required for ambient will run. This is required to run ambient mesh.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-analysis'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-analysis'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ANALYSIS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will run istio analyzers and write analysis errors to the Status field of any Istio Resources</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ca-crl'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ca-crl'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CA_CRL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If set to false, Istio will not watch for the ca-crl.pem file in the /etc/cacerts directory and will not distribute CRL data to namespaces for proxies to consume.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-cds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-cds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache CDS responses. Note: this depends on PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-cross-cluster-workload-entry'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-cross-cluster-workload-entry'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CROSS_CLUSTER_WORKLOAD_ENTRY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will read WorkloadEntry from other clusters, selectable by Services in that cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-eds-debounce'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-eds-debounce'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_DEBOUNCE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include EDS pushes in the push debouncing, configured by PILOT_DEBOUNCE_AFTER and PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX. EDS pushes may be delayed, but there will be fewer pushes. By default this is enabled</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-eds-for-headless-services'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-eds-for-headless-services'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_FOR_HEADLESS_SERVICES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, for headless service in Kubernetes, pilot will send endpoints over EDS, allowing the sidecar to load balance among pods in the headless service. This feature should be enabled if applications access all services explicitly via a HTTP proxy port in the sidecar.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, support for Kubernetes gateway-api (github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api) will  be enabled. In addition to this being enabled, the gateway-api CRDs need to be installed.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-copy-labels-annotations'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-copy-labels-annotations'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_COPY_LABELS_ANNOTATIONS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to false, istiod will not copy any attributes from the Gateway resource onto its related Deployment resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-deployment-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-deployment-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_DEPLOYMENT_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, gateway-api resources will automatically provision in cluster deployment, services, etc</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-gatewayclass-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-gatewayclass-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_GATEWAYCLASS_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, istiod will create and manage its default GatewayClasses</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-status'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-status'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_STATUS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, gateway-api resources will have status written to them</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-headless-filter-chain-listener'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-headless-filter-chain-listener'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_HEADLESS_FILTER_CHAIN_LISTENER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, headless TCP services use a single wildcard listener with per-pod /32 CIDR filter chain matches instead of one listener per pod IP. Reduces xDS size and listener count for large headless services.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ip-autoallocate'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ip-autoallocate'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_IP_AUTOALLOCATE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will start a controller that assigns IP addresses to ServiceEntry which do not have a user-supplied IP. This, when combined with DNS capture allows for tcp routing of traffic sent to the ServiceEntry.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-k8s-select-workload-entries'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-k8s-select-workload-entries'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_K8S_SELECT_WORKLOAD_ENTRIES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Kubernetes services with selectors will select workload entries with matching labels. It is safe to disable it if you are quite sure you don&#39;t need this feature</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-metadata-exchange'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-metadata-exchange'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_METADATA_EXCHANGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add metadata exchange filters, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-mongo-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-mongo-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MONGO_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>EnableMongoFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.mongo_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-multiple-custom-authz-providers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-multiple-custom-authz-providers'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MULTIPLE_CUSTOM_AUTHZ_PROVIDERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, allows multiple CUSTOM authorization providers per workload, enabling different authentication schemes (OAuth, LDAP, API keys) for different API paths. Each provider gets its own filter chain with provider-specific metadata matching.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-mysql-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-mysql-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MYSQL_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>EnableMysqlFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.mysql_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-node-untaint-controllers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-node-untaint-controllers'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_NODE_UNTAINT_CONTROLLERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, controller that untaints nodes with cni pods ready will run. This should be enabled if you disabled ambient init containers.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-persistent-session-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-persistent-session-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_PERSISTENT_SESSION_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Istiod sets up persistent session filter for listeners, if services have &#39;PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_LABEL&#39; set.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-quic-listeners'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-quic-listeners'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_QUIC_LISTENERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, QUIC listeners will be generated wherever there are listeners terminating TLS on gateways if the gateway service exposes a UDP port with the same number (for example 443/TCP and 443/UDP)</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-rds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-rds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_RDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache RDS responses. Note: this depends on PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-redis-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-redis-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_REDIS_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>EnableRedisFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.redis_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-remote-credentials-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-remote-credentials-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_REMOTE_CREDENTIALS_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will start the credentials controller for remote clusters. Default is true.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-route-collapse-optimization'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-route-collapse-optimization'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ROUTE_COLLAPSE_OPTIMIZATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will merge virtual hosts with the same routes into a single virtual host, as an optimization.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-sending-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-sending-hbone'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SENDING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE will be allowed when sending to destinations.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-serviceentry-select-pods'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-serviceentry-select-pods'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SERVICEENTRY_SELECT_PODS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, service entries with selectors will select pods from the cluster. It is safe to disable it if you are quite sure you don&#39;t need this feature</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-sidecar-listening-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-sidecar-listening-hbone'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SIDECAR_LISTENING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE support can be configured for proxies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-strict-gateway-merging'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-strict-gateway-merging'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_STRICT_GATEWAY_MERGING</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, managed GatewayAPI Gateways will not be merged with Istio Gateways from different namespaces.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-telemetry-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-telemetry-label'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_TELEMETRY_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add telemetry related metadata to cluster and endpoint resources, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-workload-entry-autoregistration'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-workload-entry-autoregistration'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_AUTOREGISTRATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Enables auto-registering WorkloadEntries based on associated WorkloadGroups upon XDS connection by the workload.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-workload-entry-healthchecks'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-workload-entry-healthchecks'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_HEALTHCHECKS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Enables automatic health checks of WorkloadEntries based on the config provided in the associated WorkloadGroup</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-xds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-xds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache XDS responses.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-xds-identity-check'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-xds-identity-check'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_IDENTITY_CHECK</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will authorize XDS clients, to ensure they are acting only as namespaces they have permissions for.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-endpoint-telemetry-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-endpoint-telemetry-label'><code>PILOT_ENDPOINT_TELEMETRY_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add telemetry related metadata to Endpoint resource, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-envoy-filter-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-envoy-filter-stats'><code>PILOT_ENVOY_FILTER_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will collect metrics for envoy filter operations.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-filter-gateway-cluster-config'>
<td><a href='#pilot-filter-gateway-cluster-config'><code>PILOT_FILTER_GATEWAY_CLUSTER_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will send only clusters that referenced in gateway virtual services attached to gateway</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-api-controller-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-api-controller-name'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_API_CONTROLLER_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/gateway-controller</code></td>
<td>Gateway API controller name. istiod will only reconcile Gateway API resources referencing a GatewayClass with this controller name</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-api-default-gatewayclass-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-api-default-gatewayclass-name'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_API_DEFAULT_GATEWAYCLASS_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio</code></td>
<td>Name of the default GatewayClass</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-transport-socket-connect-timeout'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-transport-socket-connect-timeout'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_TRANSPORT_SOCKET_CONNECT_TIMEOUT</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>15s</code></td>
<td>The timeout for transport socket (e.g., TLS handshake) connections on gateway listeners. This helps protect against slow TLS handshake attacks. Set to 0s to disable.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-hbone-initial-connection-window-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-hbone-initial-connection-window-size'><code>PILOT_HBONE_INITIAL_CONNECTION_WINDOW_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Sets the HTTP/2 initial_connection_window_size on HBONE CONNECT upstream clusters generated for waypoints and east-west gateways. If 0 (the default), the field is left unset so Envoy&#39;s built-in default applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-hbone-initial-stream-window-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-hbone-initial-stream-window-size'><code>PILOT_HBONE_INITIAL_STREAM_WINDOW_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Sets the HTTP/2 initial_stream_window_size on HBONE CONNECT upstream clusters generated for waypoints and east-west gateways. If 0 (the default), the field is left unset so Envoy&#39;s built-in default applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-http10'>
<td><a href='#pilot-http10'><code>PILOT_HTTP10</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Enables the use of HTTP 1.0 in the outbound HTTP listeners, to support legacy applications.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ignore-resources'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ignore-resources'><code>PILOT_IGNORE_RESOURCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, the resources set on this list will be ignored and never reconciled.This value should be a comma-separated list of resources names.Items on this list can be prefixed with a &#39;*.&#39; meaning a whole group should be ignored.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-include-resources'>
<td><a href='#pilot-include-resources'><code>PILOT_INCLUDE_RESOURCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, and combined with &#39;PILOT_IGNORE_RESOURCES&#39; the resources set on this list will not be ignored.This value should be a comma-separated list of resources names.Items on this list can be prefixed with a &#39;*.&#39; meaning a whole group should be included regardless of the ignore list.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-insecure-multicluster-kubeconfig-options'>
<td><a href='#pilot-insecure-multicluster-kubeconfig-options'><code>PILOT_INSECURE_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_OPTIONS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of potentially insecure kubeconfig authentication options that are allowed for multicluster authentication.Support values: all authProviders (`gcp`, `azure`, `exec`, `openstack`), `clientKey`, `clientCertificate`, `tokenFile`, and `exec`.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv4-prefix'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv4-prefix'><code>PILOT_IP_AUTOALLOCATE_IPV4_PREFIX</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>240.240.0.0/16</code></td>
<td>The CIDR range/prefix to use for auto-allocated IPv4 addresses. This should be a private range, and not conflict with any other IPs in the cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv6-prefix'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv6-prefix'><code>PILOT_IP_AUTOALLOCATE_IPV6_PREFIX</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>2001:2::/48</code></td>
<td>The CIDR range/prefix to use for auto-allocated IPv6 addresses. This should be a private range, and not conflict with any other IPs in the cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-jwt-enable-remote-jwks'>
<td><a href='#pilot-jwt-enable-remote-jwks'><code>PILOT_JWT_ENABLE_REMOTE_JWKS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Mode of fetching JWKs from JwksUri in RequestAuthentication. Supported value: istiod, false, hybrid, true, envoy. The client fetching JWKs is as following: istiod/false - Istiod; hybrid/true - Envoy and fallback to Istiod if JWKs server is external; envoy - Envoy.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-jwt-pub-key-refresh-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-jwt-pub-key-refresh-interval'><code>PILOT_JWT_PUB_KEY_REFRESH_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>20m0s</code></td>
<td>The interval for istiod to fetch the jwks_uri for the jwks public key.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-max-requests-per-second'>
<td><a href='#pilot-max-requests-per-second'><code>PILOT_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Limits the number of incoming XDS requests per second. On larger machines this can be increased to handle more proxies concurrently. If set to 0 or unset, the max will be automatically determined based on the machine size</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-multicluster-kubeconfig-path'>
<td><a href='#pilot-multicluster-kubeconfig-path'><code>PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, istiod reads remote cluster kubeconfigs from this local directory. If both `PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH` and `LOCAL_CLUSTER_SECRET_WATCHER` are set, `PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH` takes precedence.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-multi-network-discover-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-multi-network-discover-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_MULTI_NETWORK_DISCOVER_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will discover labeled Kubernetes gateway objects as multi-network gateways.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-mx-additional-labels'>
<td><a href='#pilot-mx-additional-labels'><code>PILOT_MX_ADDITIONAL_LABELS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of additional labels to be added to metadata exchange filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-node-untaint-check-ztunnel'>
<td><a href='#pilot-node-untaint-check-ztunnel'><code>PILOT_NODE_UNTAINT_CHECK_ZTUNNEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the node-untaint controller also requires ztunnel to be ready on a node before removing the readiness taint. Only applies when ambient is enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-node-untaint-controllers-taint-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-node-untaint-controllers-taint-name'><code>PILOT_NODE_UNTAINT_CONTROLLERS_TAINT_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>cni.istio.io/not-ready</code></td>
<td>The taint key used by the node-untaint controller to identify nodes that should be untainted.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-persistent-session-header-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-persistent-session-header-label'><code>PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_HEADER_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/persistent-session-header</code></td>
<td>If not empty, services with this label will use header based persistent sessions</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-persistent-session-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-persistent-session-label'><code>PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/persistent-session</code></td>
<td>If not empty, services with this label will use cookie based persistent sessions</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-prefer-sending-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-prefer-sending-hbone'><code>PILOT_PREFER_SENDING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE will be preferred when sending to destinations. </td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-push-throttle'>
<td><a href='#pilot-push-throttle'><code>PILOT_PUSH_THROTTLE</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Limits the number of concurrent pushes allowed. On larger machines this can be increased for faster pushes. If set to 0 or unset, the max will be automatically determined based on the machine size</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-remote-cluster-timeout'>
<td><a href='#pilot-remote-cluster-timeout'><code>PILOT_REMOTE_CLUSTER_TIMEOUT</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>30s</code></td>
<td>After this timeout expires, pilot can become ready without syncing data from clusters added via remote-secrets. Setting the timeout to 0 disables this behavior.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-scope-gateway-to-namespace'>
<td><a href='#pilot-scope-gateway-to-namespace'><code>PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, a gateway workload can only select gateway resources in the same namespace. Gateways with same selectors in different namespaces will not be applicable.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-send-unhealthy-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-send-unhealthy-endpoints'><code>PILOT_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include unhealthy endpoints in EDS pushes and even if they are sent Envoy does not use them for load balancing.  To avoid, sending traffic to non ready endpoints, enabling this flag, disables panic threshold in Envoy i.e. Envoy does not load balance requests to unhealthy/non-ready hosts even if the percentage of healthy hosts fall below minimum health percentage(panic threshold).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-sidecar-pick-best-service-namespace'>
<td><a href='#pilot-sidecar-pick-best-service-namespace'><code>PILOT_SIDECAR_PICK_BEST_SERVICE_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, when a sidecar needs to pick a service namespace for a hostname, it will prefer Kubernetes services and fall back to the oldest non-Kubernetes service. When disabled, the first visible namespace alphabetically is used.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-sidecar-use-remote-address'>
<td><a href='#pilot-sidecar-use-remote-address'><code>PILOT_SIDECAR_USE_REMOTE_ADDRESS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>UseRemoteAddress sets useRemoteAddress to true for sidecar outbound listeners.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-skip-validate-trust-domain'>
<td><a href='#pilot-skip-validate-trust-domain'><code>PILOT_SKIP_VALIDATE_TRUST_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Skip validating the peer is from the same trust domain when mTLS is enabled in authentication policy</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-status-max-workers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-status-max-workers'><code>PILOT_STATUS_MAX_WORKERS</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>100</code></td>
<td>The maximum number of workers Pilot will use to keep configuration status up to date.  Smaller numbers will result in higher status latency, but larger numbers may impact CPU in high scale environments.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-trace-sampling'>
<td><a href='#pilot-trace-sampling'><code>PILOT_TRACE_SAMPLING</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td>Sets the mesh-wide trace sampling percentage. Should be 0.0 - 100.0. Precision to 0.01. Default is 1.0.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-unified-sidecar-scope'>
<td><a href='#pilot-unified-sidecar-scope'><code>PILOT_UNIFIED_SIDECAR_SCOPE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, unified SidecarScope creation will be used. This is only intended as a temporary feature flag for backwards compatibility.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-workload-entry-grace-period'>
<td><a href='#pilot-workload-entry-grace-period'><code>PILOT_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_GRACE_PERIOD</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>The amount of time an auto-registered workload can remain disconnected from all Pilot instances before the associated WorkloadEntry is cleaned up.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-index-clear-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-index-clear-interval'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_INDEX_CLEAR_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>5s</code></td>
<td>The interval for xds cache index clearing.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-size'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>60000</code></td>
<td>The maximum number of cache entries for the XDS cache.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-stats'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will collect metrics for XDS cache efficiency.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='platform'>
<td><a href='#platform'><code>PLATFORM</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Platform where Istio is deployed. Possible values are &#34;openshift&#34; and &#34;gcp&#34;</td>
</tr>
<tr id='prefer-destinationrule-tls-for-external-services'>
<td><a href='#prefer-destinationrule-tls-for-external-services'><code>PREFER_DESTINATIONRULE_TLS_FOR_EXTERNAL_SERVICES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, external services will prefer the TLS settings from DestinationRules over the metadata TLS settings.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='resolve-hostname-gateways'>
<td><a href='#resolve-hostname-gateways'><code>RESOLVE_HOSTNAME_GATEWAYS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, hostnames in the LoadBalancer addresses of a Service will be resolved at the control plane for use in cross-network gateways.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='rewrite-probe-legacy-localhost-destination'>
<td><a href='#rewrite-probe-legacy-localhost-destination'><code>REWRITE_PROBE_LEGACY_LOCALHOST_DESTINATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, readiness probes will be sent to &#39;localhost&#39;. Otherwise, they will be sent to the Pod&#39;s IP, matching Kubernetes&#39; behavior.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='shared-mesh-config'>
<td><a href='#shared-mesh-config'><code>SHARED_MESH_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Additional config map to load for shared MeshConfig settings. The standard mesh config will take precedence.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='term'>
<td><a href='#term'><code>TERM</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Specifies terminal type.  Use &#39;dumb&#39; to suppress color output</td>
</tr>
<tr id='token-audiences'>
<td><a href='#token-audiences'><code>TOKEN_AUDIENCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca</code></td>
<td>A list of comma separated audiences to check in the JWT token before issuing a certificate. The token is accepted if it matches with one of the audiences</td>
</tr>
<tr id='trusted-gateway-cidr'>
<td><a href='#trusted-gateway-cidr'><code>TRUSTED_GATEWAY_CIDR</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, any connections from gateway to Istiod with this CIDR range are treated as trusted for using authentication mechanisms like XFCC. This can only be used when the network where Istiod and the authenticating gateways are running in a trusted/secure network</td>
</tr>
<tr id='unsafe-enable-admin-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#unsafe-enable-admin-endpoints'><code>UNSAFE_ENABLE_ADMIN_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, dangerous admin endpoints will be exposed on the debug interface. Not recommended for production.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='unsafe-pilot-enable-runtime-assertions'>
<td><a href='#unsafe-pilot-enable-runtime-assertions'><code>UNSAFE_PILOT_ENABLE_RUNTIME_ASSERTIONS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, addition runtime asserts will be performed. These checks are both expensive and panic on failure. As a result, this should be used only for testing.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='use-cacerts-for-self-signed-ca'>
<td><a href='#use-cacerts-for-self-signed-ca'><code>USE_CACERTS_FOR_SELF_SIGNED_CA</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will use a secret named cacerts to store its self-signed istio-generated root certificate.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='validation-webhook-config-name'>
<td><a href='#validation-webhook-config-name'><code>VALIDATION_WEBHOOK_CONFIG_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-istio-system</code></td>
<td>If not empty, the controller will automatically patch validatingwebhookconfiguration when the CA certificate changes. Only works in kubernetes environment.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='xds-auth'>
<td><a href='#xds-auth'><code>XDS_AUTH</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, will authenticate XDS clients.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='xds-auth-plaintext'>
<td><a href='#xds-auth-plaintext'><code>XDS_AUTH_PLAINTEXT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>authenticate plain text requests - used if Istiod is running on a secure/trusted network</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
