</tr>
<tr id='istio-multiroot-mesh'>
<td><a href='#istio-multiroot-mesh'><code>ISTIO_MULTIROOT_MESH</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, mesh will support certificates signed by more than one trustAnchor for ISTIO_MUTUAL mTLS</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-ipv4-loopback-cidr'>
<td><a href='#istio-outbound-ipv4-loopback-cidr'><code>ISTIO_OUTBOUND_IPV4_LOOPBACK_CIDR</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>127.0.0.1/32</code></td>
<td>IPv4 CIDR range used to identify outbound traffic on loopback interface intended for application container</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-owner-groups'>
<td><a href='#istio-outbound-owner-groups'><code>ISTIO_OUTBOUND_OWNER_GROUPS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>*</code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of groups whose outgoing traffic is to be redirected to Envoy.
A group can be specified either by name or by a numeric GID.
The wildcard character &#34;*&#34; can be used to configure redirection of traffic from all groups.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-outbound-owner-groups-exclude'>
<td><a href='#istio-outbound-owner-groups-exclude'><code>ISTIO_OUTBOUND_OWNER_GROUPS_EXCLUDE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of groups whose outgoing traffic is to be excluded from redirection to Envoy.
A group can be specified either by name or by a numeric GID.
Only applies when traffic from all groups (i.e. &#34;*&#34;) is being redirected to Envoy.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-prometheus-annotations'>
<td><a href='#istio-prometheus-annotations'><code>ISTIO_PROMETHEUS_ANNOTATIONS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-wasm-max-binary-size-bytes'>
<td><a href='#istio-wasm-max-binary-size-bytes'><code>ISTIO_WASM_MAX_BINARY_SIZE_BYTES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>268435456</code></td>
<td>Maximum size of a Wasm binary in bytes. Default is 256MB.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-watch-namespace'>
<td><a href='#istio-watch-namespace'><code>ISTIO_WATCH_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, limit Kubernetes watches to a single namespace. Warning: only a single namespace can be set.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='istio-workload-entry-validate-identity'>
<td><a href='#istio-workload-entry-validate-identity'><code>ISTIO_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_VALIDATE_IDENTITY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, will validate the identity of a workload matches the identity of the WorkloadEntry it is associating with for health checks and auto registration. This flag is added for backwards compatibility only and will be removed in future releases</td>
</tr>
<tr id='jwks-resolver-insecure-skip-verify'>
<td><a href='#jwks-resolver-insecure-skip-verify'><code>JWKS_RESOLVER_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, istiod will skip verifying the certificate of the JWKS server.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='jwt-policy'>
<td><a href='#jwt-policy'><code>JWT_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>third-party-jwt</code></td>
<td>The JWT validation policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='kubernetes-service-host'>
<td><a href='#kubernetes-service-host'><code>KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Kubernetes service host, set automatically when running in-cluster</td>
</tr>
<tr id='label-canonical-services-for-mesh-external-service-entries'>
<td><a href='#label-canonical-services-for-mesh-external-service-entries'><code>LABEL_CANONICAL_SERVICES_FOR_MESH_EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ENTRIES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, metadata representing canonical services for ServiceEntry resources with a location of mesh_external will be populatedin the cluster metadata for those endpoints.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='local-cluster-secret-watcher'>
<td><a href='#local-cluster-secret-watcher'><code>LOCAL_CLUSTER_SECRET_WATCHER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the cluster secret watcher will watch the namespace of the external cluster instead of config cluster</td>
</tr>
<tr id='max-connections-per-socket-event-loop'>
<td><a href='#max-connections-per-socket-event-loop'><code>MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_SOCKET_EVENT_LOOP</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td>The maximum number of connections to accept from the kernel per socket event. Set this to &#39;0&#39; to accept unlimited connections.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='mcs-api-group'>
<td><a href='#mcs-api-group'><code>MCS_API_GROUP</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>multicluster.x-k8s.io</code></td>
<td>The group to be used for the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) API.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='mcs-api-version'>
<td><a href='#mcs-api-version'><code>MCS_API_VERSION</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>v1alpha1</code></td>
<td>The version to be used for the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) API.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='metrics-localhost-access-only'>
<td><a href='#metrics-localhost-access-only'><code>METRICS_LOCALHOST_ACCESS_ONLY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>This will disable metrics endpoint from outside of the pod, allowing only localhost access.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='minimum-drain-duration'>
<td><a href='#minimum-drain-duration'><code>MINIMUM_DRAIN_DURATION</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>5s</code></td>
<td>The minimum duration for which agent waits before it checks for active connections and terminates proxy when number of active connections become zero</td>
</tr>
<tr id='mutex-profile-fraction'>
<td><a href='#mutex-profile-fraction'><code>MUTEX_PROFILE_FRACTION</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1000</code></td>
<td>If set to a non-zero value, enables mutex profiling a rate of 1/MUTEX_PROFILE_FRACTION events. For example, &#39;1000&#39; will record 0.1% of events. Set to 0 to disable entirely.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='output-certs'>
<td><a href='#output-certs'><code>OUTPUT_CERTS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>The output directory for the key and certificate. If empty, key and certificate will not be saved. Must be set for VMs using provisioning certificates.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='peer-metadata-discovery'>
<td><a href='#peer-metadata-discovery'><code>PEER_METADATA_DISCOVERY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If set to true, enable the peer metadata discovery extension in Envoy</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-agent-merge-envoy-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-agent-merge-envoy-stats'><code>PILOT_AGENT_MERGE_ENVOY_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If false, pilot agent will not merge Envoy stats in the agent stats endpoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-allow-any-dynamic-dns-max-hosts'>
<td><a href='#pilot-allow-any-dynamic-dns-max-hosts'><code>PILOT_ALLOW_ANY_DYNAMIC_DNS_MAX_HOSTS</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1024</code></td>
<td>Maximum number of hosts kept in the dynamic forward proxy DNS cache for ALLOW_ANY_DYNAMIC_DNS outbound traffic mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-allow-sidecar-service-inbound-listener-merge'>
<td><a href='#pilot-allow-sidecar-service-inbound-listener-merge'><code>PILOT_ALLOW_SIDECAR_SERVICE_INBOUND_LISTENER_MERGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If set, it allows creating inbound listeners for service ports and sidecar ingress listeners </td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-analysis-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-analysis-interval'><code>PILOT_ANALYSIS_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>If analysis is enabled, pilot will run istio analyzers using this value as interval in seconds Istio Resources</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-auto-allow-waypoint-policy'>
<td><a href='#pilot-auto-allow-waypoint-policy'><code>PILOT_AUTO_ALLOW_WAYPOINT_POLICY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, zTunnel will receive synthetic authorization policies for each workload ALLOW the Waypoint&#39;s identity. Unless other ALLOW policies are created, this effectively denies traffic that doesn&#39;t go through the waypoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-auto-send-unhealthy-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-auto-send-unhealthy-endpoints'><code>PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include unhealthy endpoints in EDS pushes by default. Unhealthy endpoints are excluded only when OutlierDetection is configured with minHealthPercent &gt; 0, to prevent Envoy from routing traffic to non-ready endpoints when the panic threshold is triggered.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ca-cert-configmap'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ca-cert-configmap'><code>PILOT_CA_CERT_CONFIGMAP</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca-root-cert</code></td>
<td>The name of the ConfigMap that stores the Root CA Certificate that is used by istiod</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-cert-provider'>
<td><a href='#pilot-cert-provider'><code>PILOT_CERT_PROVIDER</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istiod</code></td>
<td>The provider of Pilot DNS certificate. K8S RA will be used for k8s.io/NAME. &#39;istiod&#39; value will sign using Istio build in CA. Other values will not not generate TLS certs, but still  distribute ./etc/certs/root-cert.pem. Only used if custom certificates are not mounted.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-convert-sidecar-scope-concurrency'>
<td><a href='#pilot-convert-sidecar-scope-concurrency'><code>PILOT_CONVERT_SIDECAR_SCOPE_CONCURRENCY</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td>Deprecated, superseded by ENABLE_LAZY_SIDECAR_EVALUATION. Used to adjust the concurrency of SidecarScope conversions. When istiod is deployed on a multi-core CPU server, increasing this value will help to use the CPU to accelerate configuration push, but it also means that istiod will consume more CPU resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-crl-configmap'>
<td><a href='#pilot-crl-configmap'><code>PILOT_CRL_CONFIGMAP</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca-crl</code></td>
<td>The name of the ConfigMap that stores the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) for a plugged-in CA</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-debounce-after'>
<td><a href='#pilot-debounce-after'><code>PILOT_DEBOUNCE_AFTER</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>100ms</code></td>
<td>The delay added to config/registry events for debouncing. This will delay the push by at least this interval. If no change is detected within this period, the push will happen,  otherwise we&#39;ll keep delaying until things settle, up to a max of PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-debounce-max'>
<td><a href='#pilot-debounce-max'><code>PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>The maximum amount of time to wait for events while debouncing. If events keep showing up with no breaks for this time, we&#39;ll trigger a push.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-disable-mx-alpn'>
<td><a href='#pilot-disable-mx-alpn'><code>PILOT_DISABLE_MX_ALPN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will not put istio-peer-exchange ALPN into TLS handshake configuration.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-dns-cares-udp-max-queries'>
<td><a href='#pilot-dns-cares-udp-max-queries'><code>PILOT_DNS_CARES_UDP_MAX_QUERIES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>100</code></td>
<td>Sets the `udp_max_queries` option in Envoy for the Cares DNS resolver. Defaults to 0, an unlimited number of queries. See `extensions.network.dns_resolver.cares.v3.CaresDnsResolverConfig` in https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/extensions/network/dns_resolver/cares/v3/cares_dns_resolver.proto and `ARES_OPT_UDP_MAX_QUERIES` in https://c-ares.org/docs/ares_init.html</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-dns-jitter-duration'>
<td><a href='#pilot-dns-jitter-duration'><code>PILOT_DNS_JITTER_DURATION</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>100ms</code></td>
<td>Jitter added to periodic DNS resolution</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-draining-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-draining-label'><code>PILOT_DRAINING_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/draining</code></td>
<td>If not empty, endpoints with the label value present will be sent with status DRAINING.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-absolute-fqdn-vhost-domain'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-absolute-fqdn-vhost-domain'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ABSOLUTE_FQDN_VHOST_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If set to false, Istio will not add the absolute FQDN variant (e.g., my-service.my-ns.svc.cluster.local.) to the domains list for VirtualHost entries.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-agentgateway'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-agentgateway'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the istio-agentgateway GatewayClass will be enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-alpha-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-alpha-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, support for alpha APIs in the Kubernetes gateway-api (github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api) will  be enabled. In addition to this being enabled, the gateway-api CRDs need to be installed.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-alpn-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-alpn-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ALPN_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add Istio ALPN filters, required for proper protocol sniffing.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ambient'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ambient'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AMBIENT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, ambient mode can be used. Individual flags configure fine grained enablement; this must be enabled for any ambient functionality.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ambient-waypoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ambient-waypoints'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_AMBIENT_WAYPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, controllers required for ambient will run. This is required to run ambient mesh.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-analysis'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-analysis'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ANALYSIS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will run istio analyzers and write analysis errors to the Status field of any Istio Resources</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ca-crl'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ca-crl'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CA_CRL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If set to false, Istio will not watch for the ca-crl.pem file in the /etc/cacerts directory and will not distribute CRL data to namespaces for proxies to consume.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-cds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-cds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache CDS responses. Note: this depends on PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-cross-cluster-workload-entry'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-cross-cluster-workload-entry'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_CROSS_CLUSTER_WORKLOAD_ENTRY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will read WorkloadEntry from other clusters, selectable by Services in that cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-eds-debounce'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-eds-debounce'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_DEBOUNCE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include EDS pushes in the push debouncing, configured by PILOT_DEBOUNCE_AFTER and PILOT_DEBOUNCE_MAX. EDS pushes may be delayed, but there will be fewer pushes. By default this is enabled</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-eds-for-headless-services'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-eds-for-headless-services'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_FOR_HEADLESS_SERVICES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, for headless service in Kubernetes, pilot will send endpoints over EDS, allowing the sidecar to load balance among pods in the headless service. This feature should be enabled if applications access all services explicitly via a HTTP proxy port in the sidecar.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, support for Kubernetes gateway-api (github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api) will  be enabled. In addition to this being enabled, the gateway-api CRDs need to be installed.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-copy-labels-annotations'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-copy-labels-annotations'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_COPY_LABELS_ANNOTATIONS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to false, istiod will not copy any attributes from the Gateway resource onto its related Deployment resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-deployment-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-deployment-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_DEPLOYMENT_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, gateway-api resources will automatically provision in cluster deployment, services, etc</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-gatewayclass-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-gatewayclass-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_GATEWAYCLASS_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, istiod will create and manage its default GatewayClasses</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-gateway-api-status'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-gateway-api-status'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_GATEWAY_API_STATUS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If this is set to true, gateway-api resources will have status written to them</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-headless-filter-chain-listener'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-headless-filter-chain-listener'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_HEADLESS_FILTER_CHAIN_LISTENER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, headless TCP services use a single wildcard listener with per-pod /32 CIDR filter chain matches instead of one listener per pod IP. Reduces xDS size and listener count for large headless services.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-ip-autoallocate'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-ip-autoallocate'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_IP_AUTOALLOCATE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will start a controller that assigns IP addresses to ServiceEntry which do not have a user-supplied IP. This, when combined with DNS capture allows for tcp routing of traffic sent to the ServiceEntry.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-k8s-select-workload-entries'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-k8s-select-workload-entries'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_K8S_SELECT_WORKLOAD_ENTRIES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Kubernetes services with selectors will select workload entries with matching labels. It is safe to disable it if you are quite sure you don&#39;t need this feature</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-metadata-exchange'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-metadata-exchange'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_METADATA_EXCHANGE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add metadata exchange filters, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-mongo-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-mongo-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MONGO_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>EnableMongoFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.mongo_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-multiple-custom-authz-providers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-multiple-custom-authz-providers'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MULTIPLE_CUSTOM_AUTHZ_PROVIDERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, allows multiple CUSTOM authorization providers per workload, enabling different authentication schemes (OAuth, LDAP, API keys) for different API paths. Each provider gets its own filter chain with provider-specific metadata matching.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-mysql-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-mysql-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_MYSQL_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>EnableMysqlFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.mysql_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-node-untaint-controllers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-node-untaint-controllers'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_NODE_UNTAINT_CONTROLLERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, controller that untaints nodes with cni pods ready will run. This should be enabled if you disabled ambient init containers.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-persistent-session-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-persistent-session-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_PERSISTENT_SESSION_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Istiod sets up persistent session filter for listeners, if services have &#39;PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_LABEL&#39; set.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-quic-listeners'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-quic-listeners'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_QUIC_LISTENERS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, QUIC listeners will be generated wherever there are listeners terminating TLS on gateways if the gateway service exposes a UDP port with the same number (for example 443/TCP and 443/UDP)</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-rds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-rds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_RDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache RDS responses. Note: this depends on PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-redis-filter'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-redis-filter'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_REDIS_FILTER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>EnableRedisFilter enables injection of `envoy.filters.network.redis_proxy` in the filter chain.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-remote-credentials-controller'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-remote-credentials-controller'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_REMOTE_CREDENTIALS_CONTROLLER</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will start the credentials controller for remote clusters. Default is true.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-route-collapse-optimization'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-route-collapse-optimization'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_ROUTE_COLLAPSE_OPTIMIZATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will merge virtual hosts with the same routes into a single virtual host, as an optimization.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-sending-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-sending-hbone'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SENDING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE will be allowed when sending to destinations.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-serviceentry-select-pods'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-serviceentry-select-pods'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SERVICEENTRY_SELECT_PODS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, service entries with selectors will select pods from the cluster. It is safe to disable it if you are quite sure you don&#39;t need this feature</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-sidecar-listening-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-sidecar-listening-hbone'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_SIDECAR_LISTENING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE support can be configured for proxies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-strict-gateway-merging'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-strict-gateway-merging'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_STRICT_GATEWAY_MERGING</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, managed GatewayAPI Gateways will not be merged with Istio Gateways from different namespaces.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-telemetry-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-telemetry-label'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_TELEMETRY_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add telemetry related metadata to cluster and endpoint resources, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-workload-entry-autoregistration'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-workload-entry-autoregistration'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_AUTOREGISTRATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Enables auto-registering WorkloadEntries based on associated WorkloadGroups upon XDS connection by the workload.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-workload-entry-healthchecks'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-workload-entry-healthchecks'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_HEALTHCHECKS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Enables automatic health checks of WorkloadEntries based on the config provided in the associated WorkloadGroup</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-xds-cache'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-xds-cache'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_CACHE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will cache XDS responses.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-enable-xds-identity-check'>
<td><a href='#pilot-enable-xds-identity-check'><code>PILOT_ENABLE_XDS_IDENTITY_CHECK</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, pilot will authorize XDS clients, to ensure they are acting only as namespaces they have permissions for.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-endpoint-telemetry-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-endpoint-telemetry-label'><code>PILOT_ENDPOINT_TELEMETRY_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, pilot will add telemetry related metadata to Endpoint resource, which will be consumed by telemetry filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-envoy-filter-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-envoy-filter-stats'><code>PILOT_ENVOY_FILTER_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will collect metrics for envoy filter operations.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-filter-gateway-cluster-config'>
<td><a href='#pilot-filter-gateway-cluster-config'><code>PILOT_FILTER_GATEWAY_CLUSTER_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will send only clusters that referenced in gateway virtual services attached to gateway</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-api-controller-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-api-controller-name'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_API_CONTROLLER_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/gateway-controller</code></td>
<td>Gateway API controller name. istiod will only reconcile Gateway API resources referencing a GatewayClass with this controller name</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-api-default-gatewayclass-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-api-default-gatewayclass-name'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_API_DEFAULT_GATEWAYCLASS_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio</code></td>
<td>Name of the default GatewayClass</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-gateway-transport-socket-connect-timeout'>
<td><a href='#pilot-gateway-transport-socket-connect-timeout'><code>PILOT_GATEWAY_TRANSPORT_SOCKET_CONNECT_TIMEOUT</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>15s</code></td>
<td>The timeout for transport socket (e.g., TLS handshake) connections on gateway listeners. This helps protect against slow TLS handshake attacks. Set to 0s to disable.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-hbone-initial-connection-window-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-hbone-initial-connection-window-size'><code>PILOT_HBONE_INITIAL_CONNECTION_WINDOW_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Sets the HTTP/2 initial_connection_window_size on HBONE CONNECT upstream clusters generated for waypoints and east-west gateways. If 0 (the default), the field is left unset so Envoy&#39;s built-in default applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-hbone-initial-stream-window-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-hbone-initial-stream-window-size'><code>PILOT_HBONE_INITIAL_STREAM_WINDOW_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Sets the HTTP/2 initial_stream_window_size on HBONE CONNECT upstream clusters generated for waypoints and east-west gateways. If 0 (the default), the field is left unset so Envoy&#39;s built-in default applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-http10'>
<td><a href='#pilot-http10'><code>PILOT_HTTP10</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Enables the use of HTTP 1.0 in the outbound HTTP listeners, to support legacy applications.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ignore-resources'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ignore-resources'><code>PILOT_IGNORE_RESOURCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, the resources set on this list will be ignored and never reconciled.This value should be a comma-separated list of resources names.Items on this list can be prefixed with a &#39;*.&#39; meaning a whole group should be ignored.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-include-resources'>
<td><a href='#pilot-include-resources'><code>PILOT_INCLUDE_RESOURCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, and combined with &#39;PILOT_IGNORE_RESOURCES&#39; the resources set on this list will not be ignored.This value should be a comma-separated list of resources names.Items on this list can be prefixed with a &#39;*.&#39; meaning a whole group should be included regardless of the ignore list.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-insecure-multicluster-kubeconfig-options'>
<td><a href='#pilot-insecure-multicluster-kubeconfig-options'><code>PILOT_INSECURE_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_OPTIONS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of potentially insecure kubeconfig authentication options that are allowed for multicluster authentication.Support values: all authProviders (`gcp`, `azure`, `exec`, `openstack`), `clientKey`, `clientCertificate`, `tokenFile`, and `exec`.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv4-prefix'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv4-prefix'><code>PILOT_IP_AUTOALLOCATE_IPV4_PREFIX</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>240.240.0.0/16</code></td>
<td>The CIDR range/prefix to use for auto-allocated IPv4 addresses. This should be a private range, and not conflict with any other IPs in the cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv6-prefix'>
<td><a href='#pilot-ip-autoallocate-ipv6-prefix'><code>PILOT_IP_AUTOALLOCATE_IPV6_PREFIX</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>2001:2::/48</code></td>
<td>The CIDR range/prefix to use for auto-allocated IPv6 addresses. This should be a private range, and not conflict with any other IPs in the cluster.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-jwt-enable-remote-jwks'>
<td><a href='#pilot-jwt-enable-remote-jwks'><code>PILOT_JWT_ENABLE_REMOTE_JWKS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Mode of fetching JWKs from JwksUri in RequestAuthentication. Supported value: istiod, false, hybrid, true, envoy. The client fetching JWKs is as following: istiod/false - Istiod; hybrid/true - Envoy and fallback to Istiod if JWKs server is external; envoy - Envoy.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-jwt-pub-key-refresh-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-jwt-pub-key-refresh-interval'><code>PILOT_JWT_PUB_KEY_REFRESH_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>20m0s</code></td>
<td>The interval for istiod to fetch the jwks_uri for the jwks public key.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-max-requests-per-second'>
<td><a href='#pilot-max-requests-per-second'><code>PILOT_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Limits the number of incoming XDS requests per second. On larger machines this can be increased to handle more proxies concurrently. If set to 0 or unset, the max will be automatically determined based on the machine size</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-multicluster-kubeconfig-path'>
<td><a href='#pilot-multicluster-kubeconfig-path'><code>PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, istiod reads remote cluster kubeconfigs from this local directory. If both `PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH` and `LOCAL_CLUSTER_SECRET_WATCHER` are set, `PILOT_MULTICLUSTER_KUBECONFIG_PATH` takes precedence.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-multi-network-discover-gateway-api'>
<td><a href='#pilot-multi-network-discover-gateway-api'><code>PILOT_MULTI_NETWORK_DISCOVER_GATEWAY_API</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will discover labeled Kubernetes gateway objects as multi-network gateways.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-mx-additional-labels'>
<td><a href='#pilot-mx-additional-labels'><code>PILOT_MX_ADDITIONAL_LABELS</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Comma separated list of additional labels to be added to metadata exchange filter.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-node-untaint-check-ztunnel'>
<td><a href='#pilot-node-untaint-check-ztunnel'><code>PILOT_NODE_UNTAINT_CHECK_ZTUNNEL</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, the node-untaint controller also requires ztunnel to be ready on a node before removing the readiness taint. Only applies when ambient is enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-node-untaint-controllers-taint-name'>
<td><a href='#pilot-node-untaint-controllers-taint-name'><code>PILOT_NODE_UNTAINT_CONTROLLERS_TAINT_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>cni.istio.io/not-ready</code></td>
<td>The taint key used by the node-untaint controller to identify nodes that should be untainted.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-persistent-session-header-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-persistent-session-header-label'><code>PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_HEADER_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/persistent-session-header</code></td>
<td>If not empty, services with this label will use header based persistent sessions</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-persistent-session-label'>
<td><a href='#pilot-persistent-session-label'><code>PILOT_PERSISTENT_SESSION_LABEL</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio.io/persistent-session</code></td>
<td>If not empty, services with this label will use cookie based persistent sessions</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-prefer-sending-hbone'>
<td><a href='#pilot-prefer-sending-hbone'><code>PILOT_PREFER_SENDING_HBONE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, HBONE will be preferred when sending to destinations. </td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-push-throttle'>
<td><a href='#pilot-push-throttle'><code>PILOT_PUSH_THROTTLE</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Limits the number of concurrent pushes allowed. On larger machines this can be increased for faster pushes. If set to 0 or unset, the max will be automatically determined based on the machine size</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-remote-cluster-timeout'>
<td><a href='#pilot-remote-cluster-timeout'><code>PILOT_REMOTE_CLUSTER_TIMEOUT</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>30s</code></td>
<td>After this timeout expires, pilot can become ready without syncing data from clusters added via remote-secrets. Setting the timeout to 0 disables this behavior.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-scope-gateway-to-namespace'>
<td><a href='#pilot-scope-gateway-to-namespace'><code>PILOT_SCOPE_GATEWAY_TO_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, a gateway workload can only select gateway resources in the same namespace. Gateways with same selectors in different namespaces will not be applicable.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-send-unhealthy-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#pilot-send-unhealthy-endpoints'><code>PILOT_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, Pilot will include unhealthy endpoints in EDS pushes and even if they are sent Envoy does not use them for load balancing.  To avoid, sending traffic to non ready endpoints, enabling this flag, disables panic threshold in Envoy i.e. Envoy does not load balance requests to unhealthy/non-ready hosts even if the percentage of healthy hosts fall below minimum health percentage(panic threshold).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-sidecar-pick-best-service-namespace'>
<td><a href='#pilot-sidecar-pick-best-service-namespace'><code>PILOT_SIDECAR_PICK_BEST_SERVICE_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If enabled, when a sidecar needs to pick a service namespace for a hostname, it will prefer Kubernetes services and fall back to the oldest non-Kubernetes service. When disabled, the first visible namespace alphabetically is used.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-sidecar-use-remote-address'>
<td><a href='#pilot-sidecar-use-remote-address'><code>PILOT_SIDECAR_USE_REMOTE_ADDRESS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>UseRemoteAddress sets useRemoteAddress to true for sidecar outbound listeners.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-skip-validate-trust-domain'>
<td><a href='#pilot-skip-validate-trust-domain'><code>PILOT_SKIP_VALIDATE_TRUST_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Skip validating the peer is from the same trust domain when mTLS is enabled in authentication policy</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-status-max-workers'>
<td><a href='#pilot-status-max-workers'><code>PILOT_STATUS_MAX_WORKERS</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>100</code></td>
<td>The maximum number of workers Pilot will use to keep configuration status up to date.  Smaller numbers will result in higher status latency, but larger numbers may impact CPU in high scale environments.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-trace-sampling'>
<td><a href='#pilot-trace-sampling'><code>PILOT_TRACE_SAMPLING</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>1</code></td>
<td>Sets the mesh-wide trace sampling percentage. Should be 0.0 - 100.0. Precision to 0.01. Default is 1.0.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-unified-sidecar-scope'>
<td><a href='#pilot-unified-sidecar-scope'><code>PILOT_UNIFIED_SIDECAR_SCOPE</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, unified SidecarScope creation will be used. This is only intended as a temporary feature flag for backwards compatibility.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-workload-entry-grace-period'>
<td><a href='#pilot-workload-entry-grace-period'><code>PILOT_WORKLOAD_ENTRY_GRACE_PERIOD</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>10s</code></td>
<td>The amount of time an auto-registered workload can remain disconnected from all Pilot instances before the associated WorkloadEntry is cleaned up.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-index-clear-interval'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-index-clear-interval'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_INDEX_CLEAR_INTERVAL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>5s</code></td>
<td>The interval for xds cache index clearing.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-size'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-size'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_SIZE</code></a></td>
<td>Integer</td>
<td><code>60000</code></td>
<td>The maximum number of cache entries for the XDS cache.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pilot-xds-cache-stats'>
<td><a href='#pilot-xds-cache-stats'><code>PILOT_XDS_CACHE_STATS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If true, Pilot will collect metrics for XDS cache efficiency.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pkcs8-key'>
<td><a href='#pkcs8-key'><code>PKCS8_KEY</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Whether to generate PKCS#8 private keys</td>
</tr>
<tr id='pod-name'>
<td><a href='#pod-name'><code>POD_NAME</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr id='pod-namespace'>
<td><a href='#pod-namespace'><code>POD_NAMESPACE</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr id='prefer-destinationrule-tls-for-external-services'>
<td><a href='#prefer-destinationrule-tls-for-external-services'><code>PREFER_DESTINATIONRULE_TLS_FOR_EXTERNAL_SERVICES</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, external services will prefer the TLS settings from DestinationRules over the metadata TLS settings.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='prov-cert'>
<td><a href='#prov-cert'><code>PROV_CERT</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Set to a directory containing provisioned certs, for VMs</td>
</tr>
<tr id='proxy-config'>
<td><a href='#proxy-config'><code>PROXY_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>The proxy configuration. This will be set by the injection - gateways will use file mounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='proxy-config-xds-agent'>
<td><a href='#proxy-config-xds-agent'><code>PROXY_CONFIG_XDS_AGENT</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If set to true, agent retrieves dynamic proxy-config updates via xds channel</td>
</tr>
<tr id='resolve-hostname-gateways'>
<td><a href='#resolve-hostname-gateways'><code>RESOLVE_HOSTNAME_GATEWAYS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>If true, hostnames in the LoadBalancer addresses of a Service will be resolved at the control plane for use in cross-network gateways.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='rewrite-probe-legacy-localhost-destination'>
<td><a href='#rewrite-probe-legacy-localhost-destination'><code>REWRITE_PROBE_LEGACY_LOCALHOST_DESTINATION</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>If enabled, readiness probes will be sent to &#39;localhost&#39;. Otherwise, they will be sent to the Pod&#39;s IP, matching Kubernetes&#39; behavior.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='secret-grace-period-ratio'>
<td><a href='#secret-grace-period-ratio'><code>SECRET_GRACE_PERIOD_RATIO</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>0.5</code></td>
<td>The grace period ratio for the cert rotation, by default 0.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='secret-grace-period-ratio-jitter'>
<td><a href='#secret-grace-period-ratio-jitter'><code>SECRET_GRACE_PERIOD_RATIO_JITTER</code></a></td>
<td>Floating-Point</td>
<td><code>0.01</code></td>
<td>Randomize the grace period ratio up or down by this amount to stagger cert renewals, by default .01 (~15 minutes over 24 hours).</td>
</tr>
<tr id='secret-ttl'>
<td><a href='#secret-ttl'><code>SECRET_TTL</code></a></td>
<td>Time Duration</td>
<td><code>24h0m0s</code></td>
<td>The cert lifetime requested by istio agent</td>
</tr>
<tr id='service-account'>
<td><a href='#service-account'><code>SERVICE_ACCOUNT</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Name of service account</td>
</tr>
<tr id='shared-mesh-config'>
<td><a href='#shared-mesh-config'><code>SHARED_MESH_CONFIG</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>Additional config map to load for shared MeshConfig settings. The standard mesh config will take precedence.</td>
</tr>
<tr id='token-audiences'>
<td><a href='#token-audiences'><code>TOKEN_AUDIENCES</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>istio-ca</code></td>
<td>A list of comma separated audiences to check in the JWT token before issuing a certificate. The token is accepted if it matches with one of the audiences</td>
</tr>
<tr id='trusted-gateway-cidr'>
<td><a href='#trusted-gateway-cidr'><code>TRUSTED_GATEWAY_CIDR</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code></code></td>
<td>If set, any connections from gateway to Istiod with this CIDR range are treated as trusted for using authentication mechanisms like XFCC. This can only be used when the network where Istiod and the authenticating gateways are running in a trusted/secure network</td>
</tr>
<tr id='trust-domain'>
<td><a href='#trust-domain'><code>TRUST_DOMAIN</code></a></td>
<td>String</td>
<td><code>cluster.local</code></td>
<td>The trust domain for spiffe certificates</td>
</tr>
<tr id='unsafe-enable-admin-endpoints'>
<td><a href='#unsafe-enable-admin-endpoints'><code>UNSAFE_ENABLE_ADMIN_ENDPOINTS</code></a></td>
<td>Boolean</td>
<td><code>false</code></td>

<h3 id="pilot-discovery-completion">pilot-discovery completion</h3>

<h3 id="pilot-discovery-completion-bash">pilot-discovery completion bash</h3>

<p>This script depends on the &#39;bash-completion&#39; package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS&#39;s package manager.</p>
<p>To load completions in your current shell session:</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>source &lt;(pilot-discovery completion bash)</code></pre>
<p>To load completions for every new session, execute once:</p>

<pre class="language-bash"><code>pilot-discovery completion bash &gt; /etc/bash_completion.d/pilot-discovery</code></pre>
<h4>macOS:</h4>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>pilot-discovery completion bash &gt; /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/pilot-discovery</code></pre>
<p>You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.</p>
<pre class="language-bash"><code>pilot-discovery completion bash
